what: The constructor discovers customer, depot, visited, and location semantics from explicit fact names; resolves the exact dynamic load fluent; optionally resolves exact capacity and per-customer demand fluents; and reconstructs directed visit, return, and via-depot routing costs from grounded operator names and metric costs. At evaluation it reads the current location, visited set, and load, then performs a resource-aware nearest-neighbor rollout over unvisited customers. Each simulated step chooses the cheapest feasible direct visit or depot-reset visit, updates simulated load, and finally adds the directed return-to-depot cost. Missing optional capacity or demand information degrades permissively, and reusable state buffers avoid repeated large allocations.
why: The CVRP action structure makes a greedy completion rollout particularly useful: a chosen successor that agrees with the rollout tends to satisfy an approximate cost-to-go recursion, strongly guiding search toward coherent routes. Explicit via-depot actions naturally model route breaks, while available capacity, demand, and current load make those breaks resource-aware. Routing costs are recovered from grounded operators rather than fragile derived numeric names, preserving directed costs and generalizing across customer counts and instance values.
